Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call summary + quick clarifying questions

Hi Oliver / Sana —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so our team can scope the hosting options you asked about (hosted API vs reserved/dedicated vs private VPC/on-prem):

- FinVista's priority: keep PHI-derived inference results and user PII fully within the EU for production; APAC pilot may need a Singapore region later.
- Current constraint: procurement indicated they can sign a standard DPA if processing stays in EU regions, but cross-border processing requires additional legal review.
- Traffic profile: ~3k requests/day initially, spiky during month-end reports; typical prompt sizes 600–1,200 tokens.

Clarifying asks:
1) When you say "must stay in EU" for production, do you mean strict region residency (no egress to other clouds/regions at all) or "data-at-rest and primary processing" in EU but allowed failover to another region for availability?
2) For the APAC pilot, is it acceptable to use a Redwood-hosted APAC region (Singapore) once the DPA addendum is signed, or do you require an on-premises or private VPC in an APAC data center?

I attached a short matrix that maps hosting choices to operational implications — we'll tailor estimates once we confirm the answers above.

Next steps proposed:
- You confirm residency strictness (Q1) and APAC requirement (Q2) by Tue 12/1.
- We prepare a focused comparison (hosted EU regions vs Dedicated EU-only pools vs Private VPC in EU) with latency/cost tradeoffs and a DPA addendum draft by 12/3.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 20-minute call if that helps.

—Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Residency: Production inference must have data residency within the EU with no routine cross-border egress. Failover to non-EU regions is allowed only for disaster recovery and must be documented/approved by our legal team ahead of time.
2) APAC pilot: We prefer Redwood-hosted Singapore region for the pilot (not on-prem), but it must be isolated from the EU production workloads and clearly labeled in the contract.

We'll review the DPA addendum but believe we can proceed with your standard DPA + an EU-only clause. I'll loop in our procurement lead if we need redlines.

Also — attached our initial security questionnaire; I can upload the rest to your secure intake portal.

—Oliver

Subject: Technical notes on EU-only hosting options / latency expectations

Oliver —

Quick technical follow-up from our side after reviewing your residency requirement:

- Hosted API (Redwood-managed EU regions):
  - Pros: fastest time-to-value, automated patching, region-level data residency guarantees, built-in metrics.
  - Cons: cross-region fallback disabled by default; failover can be configured for DR but requires legal sign-off per your note.
  - Expected p95 latency (eu-west-1) for your token sizes: ~120–220ms depending on batching.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in EU-only):
  - Pros: predictable throughput, isolated capacity for compliance comfort, can be locked to EU availability zones, custom autoscaling.
  - Cons: higher committed cost; rollout lead time ~4–6 weeks.

- Private VPC / On-prem:
  - Pros: customer-managed network boundary and KMS integration; strongest control for residency.
  - Cons: longest setup (8–12 weeks on-prem), requires infra support from your side for air-gapped options.

Action items we can take this week if you confirm you want a side-by-side estimate:
- I will prepare a 6-month cost/latency projection for hosted EU vs dedicated EU-only.
- Neha will draft the minimal network diagram for a Private VPC option.

CC'ing Neha for the DPA and contract-side checklist.

—Dev
